newsitem.title: USA: Breast implant trial against Dow Chemical begins.
newsitem.headline: Breast implant trial against Dow Chemical begins.

text.p: Opening arguments were held Thusday in the much-delayed first phase of a class action lawsuit by 10,000 Louisiana women against the manufacturers of silicone breast implants which they claim are making them ill.

In the first phase, a 12-member jury will decide what role Dow Chemical Co. played in the testing and development of breast implants manufactured by Dow Corning, of which the chemical giant owns 50 percent. Claims against Dow Corning are being handled by U.S. Bankruptcy court after the company filed for protections from creditors.
Also at issue is whether Dow Chemical had any knowledge of risks that may be associated with the implants and which was withheld from doctors and consumers.
An estimated 1,600 women, recipients of breast implants manufactured by Dow Corning, are involved in that phase of the trial. Cases against other manufacturers will be tried later.

If the jury finds Dow Chemical bears some responsibility, the same jury will determine if women have been harmed by the implants and if they would have had the implants if they had been fully informed of the risks.

Calling it an important day "for the many women harmed by implants," plantiff's attorney John O'Quinn said key issues wer whether Dow Chemical, providing laboratories facilities and testing for Dow Corning, adequately tested medical products that would be put inside the human body and should last for a lifetime, and whether the company appropriately disclosed any problems discovered in testing, and when.
He said claims the devices would last for a lifetime and not leak, that they were all benefit and no risk, were untrue.
"(They) were not told that inside the body things changed, that the implants would degrade, rupture and spread threir effects through the body."
"One simple truth is that Dow Chemical was responsible for testing silicone," O'Quinn said.
Dow Chemical lead attorney Lorna Propes told jurors Dow Chemical continues "to stand with Dow Corning in saying silicone breast implants are safe, they do not make women sick. Those are the facts."

She said hundreds of tests from around the world, beginning in the 1950s, have determined that silicone is safe in the human body. "What Dow Chemical learned, it revealed. Dow Chemical performed its role properly, it hid nothing."

From the beginning, she said, doctors have known that the body responds to foreign objects by encapsulating it in tissue, and they also have known that there was some leakage by osmosis from the implants but that it was contained within the capsules of tissue.

After three hours of opening arguments, state Civil District Court Judge Yada Magee adjourned court until Wednesday, when the plaintiffs will begin presenting their case. The trial is expected to last six to eight weeks.
